brief: Q3 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth is tracking 33% year/year, matching Q2 as the strongest quarter in decades outside post-recession recoveries, but ending the acceleration pattern of recent quarters. Goldman expects 2026 EPS growth near 30% slowing to 18% in 2027. Similarly, AI capex growth is peaking: hyperscaler capex estimates held stable this season (not revised up as in prior quarters), on track for $800bn in 2026 and $1.2tn in 2027, while AI infrastructure earnings growth is seen peaking at 80% this quarter before slowing to 40% by 2027. Hyperscaler cloud revenue growth kept accelerating to 54% y/y, but crowded positioning set a high bar and hyperscalers posted negative free cash flow as capex exceeded operating cash flow. This fed renewed investor focus on AI disruption risk, including weak Alphabet search revenue, falling Reddit referral traffic, and early signs of AI-related labor-market disruption. Market breadth partially broadened via a simultaneous catch-up and catch-down: the index fell 3% even as the S&P 500 ex-AI rose 5%, cyclicals outperformed after earnings beats, and TMT beats went unrewarded.
